- Endemic schistosomiasis (demam keong) remains a public health concern in Poso Regency, Indonesia, prompting intensified government action. The program combines ecological and clinical surveillance: regular stool surveys and examinations of locally collected snail samples to map transmission. Authorities emphasize that infection can recur in people who continue activities within the snail-infested zone, making periodic re-testing essential. articleHeadline: AI Based Cough Analysis for Pulmonary Tuberculosis Triage and Diagnosis: A Technical Review - npj Biomedical Innovations
articleSummary: Pulmonary TB accounts for ~90% of TB cases; cough-based AI is explored for triage and diagnostic support. Study designs are largely retrospective/cross-sectional, focusing on TB vs non-TB, TB vs healthy, or TB vs COVID-19. articleHeadline: Lung Bacteria Found to Worsen Influenza Through a Metabolic Trap in Immune
articleSummary: Influenza A virus (IAV) severity in mouse lung models is amplified by lung microbiota dysbiosis, driven by enrichment of Bacillus cereus and its metabolite xanthosine, which downregulates nt5e (CD73) on alveolar macrophages, impairing viral phagocytosis and promoting viral replication and lung damage. articleHeadline: The Most Common Ways HIV Is Transmitted, From Sex to Needles.
articleSummary: HIV transmission occurs through specific body fluids—blood, semen, vaginal fluid, and breast milk—when they contact mucous membranes, damaged tissue, or enter the bloodstream. HIV is not transmitted by casual contact, such as handshakes, hugging, sharing meals, or saliva, nor by ordinary kisses unless deep bleeding occurs. Understanding transmission helps prevention and reduces stigma; early detection and treatment are key.

Planned actions include mass dog vaccination campaigns and dog-cropping to reduce stray populations around markets, health facilities, and schools. District leaders call for intensified community outreach, stricter enforcement of animal-control laws, and sustained vaccination funding. Residents should report stray or aggressive dogs, seek prompt medical care after bites, and participate in vaccination programs to curb transmission.

articleHeadline: ANTHRAX CASES HIT 21 IN MUCHINGA AS WILDLIFE DEATHS CLIMB TO 39 - Zambia 24
articleSummary: Anthrax outbreak in Muchinga Province, Zambia, now 21 cases after seven new infections, as wildlife deaths climb to 39 (28 hippos, 4 buffaloes, 6 elephants, 1 crocodile). Permanent Secretary Dr. Tuesday Bwalya says all patients are stable and receiving treatment in health facilities. Vaccinations are underway and livestock remain safe with no domestic cases reported so far. Officials warn against selling meat from domestic animals that die on their own before it is certified safe for consumption. Nabwalya in Mpika and surrounding districts are advised to take precautions. The PS is confident the outbreak will be contained with measures in place.
notes: 人の症例は全員安定しており治療中、家畜への感染は未確認。野生動物（カバ、バッファロー、ゾウ、ワニ）の大量死が続いており、感染源（野生動物の肉摂取）への曝露リスクが継続している点が懸念材料。ヒト-ヒト感染のリスクは低いと考えられる。
